Good morning, and welcome to our session today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you've taken this time for yourself, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As we navigate the journey of new motherhood together, I want to ensure that you feel comfortable and supported throughout our conversation.

To help us better understand how you're feeling and to provide the best possible care, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a questionnaire designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms in the postpartum period. This assessment is an important part of our care, as it allows us to identify any potential concerns early on and provide you with the necessary support and resources.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and held in the strictest confidence. My goal is to create a safe, supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings without fear of judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to listen and support you every step of the way.

Let's get started. The first question is: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. (sigh) To be honest, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty happy person, always laughing and joking around, but since having the baby, it just feels like everything is so overwhelming and serious all the time. I do still enjoy some things, like watching my baby sleep or seeing her little smile, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and laughing just doesn't come as easily as it used to. I might crack a smile every now and then, but it's not like I'm really feeling it, you know? It's like I'm just pretending to be happy, but deep down, I'm just feeling really tired and sad. (pausing, looking down) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No... I don't think so. Like I said, it's just been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I might laugh at something my husband says or a funny video, but it's not like it's coming from a genuinely happy place. It's more like I'm just trying to be polite or pretend like everything is okay when it's not. (sighing) Most of the time, I just feel anxious or worried about something, and it's hard for me to shake that off and just laugh and have a good time. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) Does that sound crazy.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really... I mean, I used to love doing things like going out with friends, trying new restaurants, or just relaxing at home with a good book. But now, everything just feels like so much work. Even things that I used to enjoy, like taking a shower or getting dressed, just feel like chores. (sighing) I don't really look forward to things like I used to. Most of the time, I just feel like I'm trying to get through the day, you know? Take care of the baby, make sure everyone is fed and happy... it's just exhausting. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or watching a movie, but then I'll just think about all the things I need to do instead, and it feels too overwhelming. (shrugging) I don't know, it's just hard to find the motivation to do things that used to bring me joy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah... I do that a lot. I mean, if the baby is crying and I'm trying to figure out what's wrong, I'll start thinking that it's my fault, that I'm not doing something right. Or if I'm feeling really overwhelmed and I need to ask for help, I'll think that I'm a bad mom for not being able to handle it on my own. (sighing) It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's just this constant voice in my head telling me that I'm not good enough, that I'm making mistakes. Even when my husband or family members try to reassure me, it's hard to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-doubt. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) Like, the other day, I was trying to get the baby to sleep, and I was getting really frustrated because she just wouldn't settle down. And then I started thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I even get this right?" (shaking head) It's just really hard to be kind to myself and not blame myself for everything that goes wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yeah... all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all these worst-case scenarios. Like, what if she stops breathing? What if I'm not feeding her enough? What if someone breaks into the house and hurts us? (shuddering) It's just this constant stream of anxious thoughts that I don't know how to turn off. And the worst part is, I know they're not rational. I mean, I'm a good mom, I'm taking care of her, but my brain just won't stop worrying. (rubbing temples) Sometimes it feels like my mind is just racing and I don't know how to calm it down. And it's not just during the day, either. At night, when I'm trying to sleep, all these worries just come flooding back and it's hard to fall asleep. (sighing) I feel like I'm just constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. (looking up, eyes wide with concern) Does that sound crazy?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yeah... that's happened to me too. Like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (placing a hand on chest) It's hard to describe, but it's like this feeling of intense fear or dread, and I don't know what's causing it. It's not like I'm thinking about anything specific, it's just this overwhelming sense of anxiety. (shaking head) And it's scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll try to take some deep breaths, or distract myself with something else, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's like, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start thinking, "What if something happens to me? What if I'm not here to take care of her?" (voice cracking) And then I'll just feel this wave of fear, and I don't know how to calm myself down. (taking a deep breath, trying to compose herself) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about this stuff.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yeah... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to be a good partner and friend... it's all just so overwhelming. (sighing) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be doing okay, and then something will happen, like the baby will start crying, or I'll realize I forgot to do something important, and it's just like... (throwing hands up in the air) everything comes crashing down. (shaking head) I feel like I'm just trying to survive, you know? Like, I'm not really living, I'm just trying to make it through each day without too much chaos. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to handle it all. I should be able to be a good mom, and a good partner, and a good person... but it's just so hard. (wiping away tears) Sorry, I'm just... it's all just really hard right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... that's me. I mean, I'm so exhausted all the time, but when I try to sleep, my mind just won't shut off. I'll be lying there, thinking about all the things I need to do, or worrying about the baby, or just feeling overwhelmed and sad... and I just can't seem to relax. (sighing) Some nights, I'll wake up like five or six times, just because I'm having anxious thoughts or I'm worried about something. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I feel like I'm just running on empty all the time. (rubbing eyes) It's hard to explain, but it's like... my brain is just constantly "on", you know? Like, I'm always thinking about something, or worrying about something, and it's just hard to turn that off. (shaking head) And it's not just the lack of sleep, it's the feeling of being unhappy and overwhelmed that's just always there, lurking in the background. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just stuck in this never-ending cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to escape.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... that's me. I feel like I've been sad or miserable for so long now. It's like, I'll have these little moments of happiness, like when the baby smiles at me or something, but they're just fleeting. Most of the time, I just feel this deep sense of sadness and emptiness. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like... I feel like I've lost myself, you know? Like, I'm just a mom now, and I don't know who I am outside of that. (looking down) And it's not just the sadness, it's the feeling of being overwhelmed and anxious all the time. It's like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, or for someone to tell me that I'm not doing a good enough job. (shaking head) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and it's exhausting. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll just be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, I just feel so sad and overwhelmed. (wiping away tears) It's like, I'm just trying to survive, but I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... that's me. I cry all the time. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. I don't even know what's triggering it, it's just like... everything is just too much, and I feel so overwhelmed. (sobbing) I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, or just sitting there, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm just so sad, and I don't know how to make it stop. (wiping away tears) Sometimes I'll try to hold it in, but it's just too hard. I'll be talking to my husband, or a friend, and I'll just start crying. It's so embarrassing, but I just can't help it. (shaking head) I feel like I'm just losing control, like I'm just barely holding on. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too. Like, if the baby is crying, and I don't know how to calm her down, I'll just start crying. Or if I'm feeling overwhelmed, and I don't know how to ask for help, I'll just start crying. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) It's like, I'm just so tired of feeling this way, but I don't know how to make it stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Yes... I'm ashamed to admit it, but yes. There have been times when I've felt so overwhelmed, so trapped, that I've thought about... (pausing, struggling to get the words out) ...about harming myself. It's not that I really want to, it's just that sometimes it feels like the only way to escape the pain and the sadness. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) But I don't think I could ever actually do it. I mean, I have the baby to think about, and my husband, and... (shaking head) I don't know, it's just that sometimes it feels like the only way to make the pain stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's not something I've thought about a lot, but it's been there, lurking in the back of my mind. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) I'm scared to admit it, because I don't want anyone to think I'm crazy, or that I'm a bad mom. But... (pausing, looking up) I guess I just needed to be honest. (tears streaming down face) I don't know what's wrong with me, or how to make it stop. I just feel so lost and alone.

The patient has expressed a range of emotional and behavioral concerns that are consistent with postpartum depression and anxiety, including persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of pleasure in activities, difficulty coping with daily responsibilities, anxiety, panic, and worry about the baby's well-being and own ability to care for them, sleep difficulties, frequent crying spells, and feelings of guilt and worthlessness.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 29, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient states they don't think they can laugh and see the funny side of things, and that even when they do laugh, it's not from a genuinely happy place, indicating a significant inability to laugh and see the funny side of things.</sym>, <sym>Patient states they don't really look forward to things like they used to, and everything feels like too much work, indicating a significant decrease in enjoyment and motivation.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a frequent pattern of self-blame, stating they do it 'a lot' and describing a 'constant voice in their head' telling them they're not good enough, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports being anxious or worried 'all the time', with a 'constant stream of anxious thoughts' that they can't turn off, indicating a high frequency of anxiety, matching the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense feelings of panic and fear without a specific reason, using phrases like 'wave of panic', 'intense fear or dread', and 'overwhelming sense of anxiety', indicating a high level of distress.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong feeling of being overwhelmed and struggling to cope with daily responsibilities, suggesting they haven't been able to cope at all most of the time.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes persistent unhappiness, difficulty sleeping, and an inability to relax due to overwhelming thoughts and anxiety, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they feel sad or miserable most of the time, with only fleeting moments of happiness, and experiences a deep sense of sadness and emptiness, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of harming herself, but emphasizes it's not something she's thought about a lot and doesn't think she could actually do it, which aligns with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses suggest a high risk for postpartum depression and anxiety, characterized by persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, consistent with <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med> as outlined in the <med>DSM-5</med>. The presence of self-harm thoughts is a significant safety concern that requires immediate attention. The patient's EPDS score of 29 falls into the probable depression category, which necessitates an urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if experiencing suicidal thoughts
3. Develop a safety plan with the patient to ensure their well-being and the well-being of their baby
4. Provide patient with resources for postpartum depression and anxiety support groups
5. Encourage patient to engage in self-care activities, such as exercise, meditation, and spending time with loved ones
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
